cards.text: Korah, a Levite, led a rebellion against Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron, the priest. The LORD judged the rebels, but the very next day the people grumbled against Moses and Aaron ANYWAY (Numbers 16). Now the LORD speaks to Moses.
God's plan is simple. Moses is to collect staffs from the Israelites, one from the leader of each tribe.

cards.question: One staff per tribe leader means Moses collects ___ staffs.
Each tribe leader's name gets written on his own staff.
The tribe of Levi gets a staff too. God says the staff of Levi gets ___'s name on it.

cards.text: All the staffs go into the Tent of Meeting, in front of the Testimony, where God meets with Moses. Sticks in a tent. Either a miracle's coming or somebody's going CAMPING.

cards.question: God says the staff of the man He chooses will do something. What will it do?

answers.text: It will turn into a snake

cards.question: God tells Moses the sprouting staff will rid Him of "the constant grumbling of the Israelites against you."

cards.text: Moses gathers all twelve staffs, Aaron's among them, and lays them before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony. The next day, he walks back in.

cards.question: One of the twelve staffs in the tent has changed. Whose staff is it?
Aaron's staff isn't just a stick anymore. What does Moses find on it?

cards.text: Moses brings all twelve staffs out for all the Israelites to see, and each leader takes his own back. Friend, I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS and grew nothing but DUST, and this staff grew ALMONDS by the next day.

cards.question: Then the LORD gives orders about Aaron's staff. Moses is to hand it back to Aaron to carry.
Instead, Aaron's staff goes back in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign. Who is the sign for?
When God explains the sign, He says the people's grumbling is against Him.
God says the sign will put an end to the people's grumbling against Him. Why does He want it to end?

cards.text: Moses does exactly what the LORD commands, no arguing, no snooze button. Now that sign for the rebellious sits in front of the Testimony, and the Israelites come to Moses.

cards.question: What do the Israelites cry out to Moses after seeing Aaron's staff?

answers.text: That they are all lost and perishing
That they will gladly follow Aaron
That they want to go back to Egypt

cards.question: The Israelites tell Moses that anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will ___.

cards.text: Then they ask Moses, "Are we all going to perish?" We'll let that question hang right there for now, friend, because this story still has pages left.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "All the staffs go into the Tent of Meeting... where God meets with Moses." "Sticks in a tent." "Either a miracle's coming or somebody's going CAMPING." Story cards after the opening card can have only 1 or 2 sentences. Fold the joke into one sentence or trim it.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question asks which thing Moses finds on the staff, so the wrong answers must be real Bible details. "Moss" and "pinecones" aren't Bible details. "Thorns and moss and pinecones" also sounds sillier than the other answers. Use real biblical plant details, like figs, pomegranates or olives.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The card cites only Numbers 17:11, but it also tells "and the Israelites come to Moses," which comes from Numbers 17:12. The citation should be Numbers 17:11-12. Or remove that clause so the card only tells 17:11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Several story cards are plain narration with no Papa Dorin energy. Card 2 ("God's plan is simple...") and card 9 (Moses gathers the staffs and walks back in the next day) are examples. Card 9 is a natural place for a real laugh, since the next-day reveal is coming. Only cards 6, 12 and 17 carry a joke, and card 17's is a quick aside. The walkthrough reads more like a nice dad being pleasant than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
